rules.statement: Don't enable HTTP logging of request or response bodies, the query string or trailers through configuration or global `HttpLoggingOptions.LoggingFields` (for example `HttpLoggingFields.All`); log only request and response properties, allow-listed headers and duration, and allow a body only through a per-endpoint opt-in in code.
rules.why: Bodies and query strings carry secrets, codes, tokens and passwords, and a log level or setting is an operator's dial, so any protection that depends on configuration is none; a reviewed per-endpoint opt-in in code is the only safe gate.
rules.check: Look for `LoggingFields` set to include `RequestBody`, `ResponseBody`, `RequestQuery`, `RequestTrailers`, `ResponseTrailers` or `All`, or a configuration section that turns body logging on.

rules.statement: Never add `Authorization`, `Proxy-Authorization`, `Cookie`, `DPoP`, `Set-Cookie` or `Location` to an HTTP logging header allow-list, and remove `Location` from the framework's default response-header allow-list.
rules.why: These headers carry credentials, and a `Location` can carry an authorization code; the framework's default response allow-list includes `Location`.
rules.check: Look at `RequestHeaders`/`ResponseHeaders` changes on `HttpLoggingOptions` and confirm none of these headers is added and `Location` is removed.

rules.statement: Never opt an endpoint whose request or response bodies carry credentials, tokens, passwords, secrets or user claims into body logging, and mark such endpoints as confidential at the route-group level rather than one endpoint at a time.
rules.why: Marking a route group fails safe: a missed or later-added endpoint inherits the mark, whereas per-endpoint marking lets a new endpoint slip through and opt in.
rules.check: For a new endpoint or group that opts in to body logging, check whether it handles credentials; for a new credential-bearing group, check it carries the confidential mark on the group, not only on individual endpoints.

rules.statement: Don't use `[HttpLogging]` or `WithHttpLogging(...)` endpoint metadata to enable body, query or credential-header logging on an endpoint.
rules.why: The framework's endpoint metadata can enable any field, the query string included, on any endpoint, a credential-bearing one too, so it is stripped and is not an acceptable opt-in.
rules.check: Look for `[HttpLogging(...)]` attributes or `.WithHttpLogging(...)` calls in endpoint mapping code.

rules.statement: Call `UseHttpLogging()` immediately after `UseRouting()` in the middleware pipeline.
rules.why: The middleware sees endpoint metadata, such as a body opt-in or confidential mark, only after routing has selected the endpoint.
rules.check: In host startup, verify `UseHttpLogging()` follows `UseRouting()` and is not placed before it.

rules.statement: Cap the `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Hosting.Diagnostics` logger at `Warning` with a rule that applies to every logging provider, so a provider-scoped level such as `Logging:Console:LogLevel` cannot raise it.
rules.why: Its `Request starting` and `Request finished` lines log the full URL including the query string, which carries codes and `id_token_hint`, outside HTTP logging.
rules.check: Look for logging configuration or filter code that raises `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Hosting.Diagnostics` to Information or below, or a cap that is scoped to one provider only.

rules.statement: Validate logging-safety options when the host starts in every environment, not only in Production.
rules.why: Development and Staging logs are shipped by collectors too, so a Production-only refusal leaves them open.
rules.check: Look for a check that refuses unsafe logging options guarded by an environment condition such as `IsProduction()`.

rules.statement: Fail when the endpoints are built, with an `InvalidOperationException` naming the endpoint, if an endpoint is both marked as carrying confidential bodies and opted in to body logging.
rules.why: A conflicting mark and opt-in must never quietly resolve to logging credentials. Failing at build time with the endpoint's name surfaces the mistake straight away.
rules.check: In endpoint convention or metadata code that combines the confidential mark with a body opt-in, confirm the conflict throws rather than picking one setting silently.
